method: Edge-chained word table, fitted on the public practice training pages only, with no grammar or meaning. Two tables are counted from the training pages: for every pair of adjacent certain words within a line, how often each first glyph follows each last glyph (eva-basic glyphs); and, for each first glyph, the certain words that begin with it with their frequencies. Text is written word by word: draw the next word's first glyph from the first table given the previous word's last glyph, then draw a word beginning with that glyph from the second table by frequency (seed 2026, 40,000 words, cut into lines of ten; the scorer re-cuts them to the hidden line shapes). The writer never sees line breaks or meaning; it only carries one glyph of memory from word to word, which a scribe choosing each next word to start with a glyph that suits the previous ending could do with two tally sheets. On the practice split the fact holds on this text (0.244 against 0.230 for the manuscript) with no four-word run copied.
